title: Awards Venezuela Oil Licenses to Firms With Bribery Records
description_short: The administration granted licenses to global traders with prior bribery cases to sell sanctioned Venezuelan oil, sparking transparency and corruption concerns.
description_medium: On January 29, 2026, the Trump administration awarded licenses to global trading firms with prior bribery cases to sell sanctioned Venezuelan oil. The awards drew concerns about transparency and the selection of companies with bribery histories. The license holders and terms are not specified, and the firms’ past cases are not linked to these oil transactions.
description_long:
On January 29, 2026, the Trump administration awarded licenses to global trading firms with prior bribery cases to sell Venezuelan oil covered by U.S. sanctions. The awards drew concerns about transparency and the choice of companies with bribery histories. Because licenses determine which firms may handle sanctioned-oil sales, the selection process and safeguards attached to the permissions became central questions.

The license holders, license conditions, volume and value of oil, and official selection rationale are not specified. The firms’ earlier bribery cases are not described or connected to these Venezuelan transactions. That distinction matters: the reported concern is about granting oil-sale authority to companies with bribery histories, while the facts do not establish that the licensing decision itself was corrupt or that new bribery occurred.

Without those details, the extent of any financial benefit to the traders and the oversight applied to these sales cannot be determined. The supported account is a contested licensing decision involving sanctioned oil and firms with prior bribery cases.

title: Trump Urges SAVE America Act Requiring Proof of Citizenship to Vote
description_short: Trump asked Congress to pass the SAVE America Act to require proof of citizenship for voting.
description_medium: At the February 25, 2026 State of the Union, President Donald Trump urged Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to vote. His request was a proposal and did not change voting rules by itself. The speech account gives no list of accepted documents or later legislative status.
description_long:
During his February 25, 2026 State of the Union address, President Donald Trump urged Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, described as requiring proof of citizenship to vote. The request placed a proposed national voting rule before lawmakers; it did not itself change voter-registration requirements. Congress would have to enact the bill before such a requirement could take effect.

The available account does not state which documents the bill would accept, whether it includes exceptions, or what legislative progress followed the speech. It also provides no estimate of how many voters might need additional documentation. Those details matter to any assessment of the proposal’s practical reach. The event supports saying that Trump advocated a proof-of-citizenship requirement, but not that the requirement became law or that voters experienced a particular consequence.

The distinction between advocacy and enacted policy is central here: the action recorded is a request to Congress, while the legal effect remained contingent on legislation.
